stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: In 2019, astronomers monitoring a dim red dwarf in the constellation Lyra noticed that its brightness fell by about 0.4 percent every 11.2 days. Starspots can cause such dips, but spots drift and fade as a star rotates. The strict regularity of the dips and the unchanging depth of each one across nearly three years of ______ the team that an orbiting planet was passing in front of the star.
explanation: The subject is long: 'The strict regularity of the dips and the unchanging depth of each one across nearly three years of observation.' Its verb is 'convinced.' No punctuation goes between a subject and its verb, however long the subject is. With no punctuation, the sentence reads as one main clause.

A.why: The long subject made you want to pause before the verb. A single comma never separates a subject from its verb, and nothing earlier in the sentence opens an interruption that this comma could be closing.

B.why: You used a semicolon, which needs a complete sentence on each side. The text before it is only a subject, and the text after it is a verb with no subject, so both sides are fragments.

D.why: You treated the dash as a pause for emphasis. A single dash works like a colon and needs a complete sentence before it, but here it cuts the subject off from its verb 'convinced.'

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Runners often slow down in the last stage of a marathon, but coaches disagree about why. In a 2022 study of 140 recreational marathoners, exercise physiologists ______ much each runner's stride length shortened over the final ten kilometers and how strongly that shortening predicted finishing time. Stride length, they found, explained more of the late slowdown than heart rate did.
explanation: 'Measured' is a verb, and its object is the pair of 'how' clauses that follows ('how much... and how strongly...'). No punctuation goes between a verb and its object, so the correct choice leaves the space empty.

B.why: The two 'how' clauses looked like a list, so you reached for a colon. A colon needs a complete sentence before it, and 'exercise physiologists measured' is incomplete without its object.

C.why: The long object made you want to take a breath after the verb. A comma should not separate 'measured' from what was measured.

D.why: You used a semicolon, which needs a complete sentence on each side. Neither side stands alone: the verb is missing its object, and the 'how' clauses have no main verb.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Economists have long disagreed about whether raising the minimum wage reduces employment. A 2021 analysis of payroll records from 300 counties found little change in overall job numbers after wage increases. It did, however, identify the one ______ the policy appeared to hurt: full-service restaurants, where owners cut staff hours rather than positions.
explanation: 'That the policy appeared to hurt' tells you which sector the analysis identified. It is an essential clause, so it takes no punctuation before it. The complete clause 'It did, however, identify the one sector that the policy appeared to hurt' then correctly sets up the colon.

A.why: You treated the 'that' clause as optional extra information. It defines which sector is meant, and an essential 'that' clause is never set off with a comma.

B.why: You used a dash to add emphasis. A dash splits 'sector' from the clause that identifies it, leaving 'the one sector' without its definition.

C.why: You used a semicolon, which needs a complete sentence on each side. 'That the policy appeared to hurt' cannot stand alone, and 'identify the one sector' is left without its essential modifier.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Evidence of early brewing is hard to confirm, because many residues left by fermented drinks also form during ordinary cooking. At a Bronze Age settlement in northern Spain, however, excavators recovered both sprouted barley grains from a sealed storage pit beneath the eastern ______ fragments of a perforated clay vessel bearing traces of oxalate, a compound that builds up during fermentation.
explanation: 'Both' signals a paired construction: 'both sprouted barley grains... and fragments of a perforated clay vessel.' The two halves are noun phrases that together form the object of 'recovered.' Nothing separates them, so 'and' needs no punctuation before it.

A.why: The first noun phrase was long, so you added a comma before 'and.' That comma belongs before 'and' only when it joins two complete sentences. Here 'and' joins two parts of a 'both... and' pair, and a comma cannot split them.

C.why: You used a semicolon, which needs a complete sentence on each side. The text after it, 'and fragments of a perforated clay vessel...,' has no verb and cannot stand alone.

D.why: You used a colon as though it introduced an explanation. A colon cannot break into the middle of a 'both... and' pair, and the sentence before it is still waiting for its second item.

explanation: The subject is 'The observation that such children often combine the grammar of one language with the vocabulary of the other,' and its verb is 'was taken.' B.why: The subject ends a long 'that' clause, so it felt as if something needed closing. No comma opened this clause, so there is nothing to close, and one comma between a subject and its verb is incorrect.

C.why: You used a semicolon, which needs a complete sentence on each side. The first side is only a subject, and 'was taken as proof...' has no subject of its own.

D.why: You used a dash to mark the end of the long subject. A single dash needs a complete sentence before it, and this one would separate the subject from its verb.

stimulus: Planting two crops together in the same field, a practice called intercropping, can reduce a farm's need for fertilizer. Compared with oats planted alone, the mixture gave ______ 18 percent more total grain per hectare while requiring no added nitrogen.
explanation: 'Gave' takes two objects here. 'Farmers' is who received something, and 'roughly 18 percent more total grain' is what they received. No punctuation goes between a verb and its objects, so both run straight on from 'gave.'

A.why: The number felt like a new unit, so you paused before it. A comma here separates 'gave farmers' from what the farmers were given, splitting the verb from its object.

B.why: You used a colon to introduce the result. A colon needs a complete sentence before it, and 'the mixture gave farmers' is incomplete because it never says what was given.

C.why: You used a semicolon, which needs a complete sentence on each side. 'Roughly 18 percent more total grain...' has no verb, and the clause before it is missing its object.

stimulus: The tale of the clever miller's daughter survives in more than two hundred recorded versions from across central Europe. In most of them, she outwits a greedy landlord with the help of an animal companion. Whether that companion was a fox or a hare in the earliest oral ______ folklorists, since the two oldest written versions, set down within a decade of each other, disagree.
explanation: The whole clause 'Whether that companion was a fox or a hare in the earliest oral tellings' is the subject, and 'still divides' is its verb. A 'whether' clause acting as a subject connects to its verb with no punctuation.

A.why: You read the 'whether' clause as an introductory phrase, like one beginning with 'if,' and set it off with a comma. It is the subject of 'divides,' and a comma cannot separate a subject from its verb.

B.why: You used a semicolon, which needs a complete sentence on each side. The 'whether' clause has no main verb of its own, and 'still divides folklorists' has no subject.

D.why: You used a dash to mark the end of the long question. A single dash needs a complete sentence before it, and this one splits the subject from its verb.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Medieval European dyers prized kermes, a red dye made from the dried bodies of scale insects, but it cost far more than madder, a dye made from plant roots. Many surviving red textiles were therefore assumed to be madder-dyed. When conservators tested a fourteenth-century tapestry fragment held in a Flemish archive, however, chemical analysis ______ the red threads had been colored with kermes throughout.
explanation: 'That the red threads had been colored with kermes throughout' is what the analysis revealed, so it is the object of the verb 'revealed.' A verb and its 'that' clause object connect with no punctuation.

A.why: The commas around 'however' earlier in the sentence made you expect another break. Those commas are already a complete pair. A comma here would separate 'revealed' from its object.

C.why: You used a colon to introduce the finding. A colon needs a complete sentence before it, and 'chemical analysis revealed' is incomplete without saying what was revealed.

D.why: You used a semicolon, which needs a complete sentence on each side. 'That the red threads had been colored with kermes' cannot stand alone, and the clause before it is missing its object.
